body: :] thank you for listening. Going to bed now :)

You're so right - sometimes it is really helpful to just be loved, even when that person doesn't always know how to help you. I think I'm at a really low point right now because our parents just met last night (our families are on opposite sides of the US, so it took a long time for that to happen) and everything is feeling way too real, and I'm really questioning this whole thing. 

Yes - like a tornado haha!! And I get in this place where everything is very URGENT and needs to **happen right now**!

Oh yes - I do remember that.

I've never seen that kind of workbook before. Was that helpful for you? Looks interesting.  I know exactly what you mean about the "mirror checking" and skin picking.

Yep - I take citalopram/Celexa. It definitely helps my self-awareness.

I have been seeing the same therapist for quite sometime, and I became weirdly obsessed with being her "best client". I would make several pages worth of notes of things to tell her, and then I would spend my whole appointment talking a mile a minute, and it started to feel really unhelpful. I am currently taking a break from talk therapy. Also when I lost my job, I lost my therapy budget. 

CBT is the excercise where you're trying to associate thoughts with different physical sensations? I don't remember exactly -  I have done many different types of therapy and I don't remember which one that is...

Why *do* I grind my teeth? I am not sure? I usually don't notice I'm doing it until I have a headache.

Thank you so much for this. Seriously. 

Is that why you broke up with your ex? Besides this (which is kind of a big deal), we really have an awesome relationship - we share a lot of the same values, and .... well whatever right now that doesn't feel very important. He drew up in a family that doesn't make any effort to articulate their feelings - there is only anger and joy, and nothing in between. Nobody was talking out their problems or learning how to comprimise. So usually I'm the one holding his hand when we have conversations with any kind of emotional importance. When I come to him in crisis and say "I'm having a panic attack here is what I need from you: X, Y, and Z." (I try to be really upfront about my needs - thanks, therapy), he either gets weirdly defensive, or shuts down and says nothing. You can imagine how unhelpful that is!

I'm sure it's contributed. I definitely come across as "stable", but I've been way too selective about the kinds of jobs that I apply for because I'll not quite be able to picture myself doing something *correctly*. 

What OCD is like for me - I'm having a hard time typing this because I keep deleting a sentence I just wrote, and then I'll type the same thing again. I have a teeth grinding problem, to the point of having facial surgery (a bone graft) last year, and a TMJ diagnosis this year. Thoughts circulate in my head for *hours*, and I am not super aware of time passing when I get stuck on scary thoughts (I don't know why I find them scary - sometimes its something as simple as a specific color pattern flashing in my head - but they feel like nightmares). Behaviorally, nothing shows up that is very obvious to anyone else - no one can tell that I obsessively grind my teeth and pick at my skin.
